findings.evidence: maintenance documentation will be supplied and the operating system will be tested
findings.rationale: Uses passive voice without specifying whether Yoggie Corporation or the Web Store developers are responsible for supplying maintenance documentation and testing the operating system.

findings.evidence: Must use a SQL based database.
findings.rationale: Repeats the SQL-based database requirement already stated in GJ-003 without adding distinct functional scope.

findings.evidence: Other versions may not be 100% compatible. Also other browsers such as Mozilla or Firefox may not be 100% compatible.
findings.rationale: Uses non-binding 'may' and open-ended 'such as', leaving required behavior and compatibility expectations for unsupported browser versions and other browsers unclear.

findings.evidence: Compatibility is only tested and verified for Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6 and 7, Netscape Communicator Version 4 and 5.
findings.rationale: Uses passive voice without specifying which party or component is responsible for testing and verifying browser compatibility.

findings.evidence: Compatibility is only tested and verified for Microsoft Internet Explorer version 6 and 7, Netscape Communicator Version 4 and 5.
findings.rationale: Restates the same supported browser list (Microsoft Internet Explorer 6 and 7, Netscape Communicator 4 and 5) already specified in GJ-001.

findings.evidence: Shall install online help for users via the web interface
findings.rationale: Omits the subject/actor responsible for installing online help (e.g., the system, installer, administrator, or developers).

findings.evidence: Operations and Maintenance manual, Users Guide book, and Installation Instructions for the Administrator.
findings.rationale: Prepositional phrase attachment is ambiguous: 'for the Administrator' could apply only to 'Installation Instructions' or to all three manuals (including 'Users Guide book').

findings.evidence: Shall deliver Operations and Maintenance manual, Users Guide book, and Installation Instructions for the Administrator.
findings.rationale: Omits the actor responsible for delivering the documentation (e.g., Web Store developers or Yoggie Corporation).

findings.evidence: will do periodic backups
findings.rationale: 'periodic' is unquantified with no testable backup frequency, and 'will' is weaker than mandatory 'shall'.

findings.evidence: periodic backups through a live internet connection
findings.rationale: References periodic backups without specifying the backup interval value/unit or retention policy, and omits error handling if the live internet connection is unavailable.

findings.evidence: The system shall validate credit cards against fraud.
findings.rationale: Specifies credit card fraud validation without defining the system behavior when fraud is detected or validation fails (e.g., rejecting the transaction, notifying the customer/administrator, or logging the attempt).

findings.evidence: sensitive information
findings.rationale: 'sensitive information' is subjective and undefined, leaving unclear which specific data elements must be encrypted over HTTPS.

findings.evidence: auto detect IP DOS attacks and block IP automatically
findings.rationale: Does not specify the block timeout duration or unblocking/recovery procedure after an IP is blocked, nor the quantitative traffic threshold defining an IP DOS attack.

findings.evidence: The system shall detect consecutive failed login attempts.
findings.rationale: Specifies a detection condition without defining any resulting system action (e.g., lockout, alert, cooldown) or the numeric threshold of consecutive failed attempts.

findings.evidence: the system shall validate 'existing' credit card in system after each log in
findings.rationale: Specifies credit card validation on login without defining what happens if the stored card is invalid, expired, or fails validation.

findings.evidence: too large in size
findings.rationale: 'too large in size' is subjective and provides no measurable criterion for when image compression must occur.

findings.evidence: automatically compress image files that are too large in size
findings.rationale: References a file-size limit without giving the numeric threshold and unit (e.g., KB or MB) or the target compressed size/quality.

findings.evidence: will employ on demand asynchronous loading for faster execution of pages
findings.rationale: 'faster execution of pages' is an unquantified comparative claim with no baseline or target load time, and 'will' is non-mandatory compared to 'shall'.

findings.evidence: The system shall validate email address existence.
findings.rationale: Describes an email existence validation check without specifying the error handling when the email address does not exist or verification fails.

findings.evidence: easy to use
findings.rationale: 'easy to use' is subjective and unquantified, offering no measurable usability criterion.

findings.evidence: easy to learn
findings.rationale: 'easy to learn' is subjective and unquantified, lacking any measurable learnability target (e.g., training duration or task success rate).

findings.evidence: easy to locate buttons
findings.rationale: 'easy to locate' is subjective and provides no testable UI layout or discoverability standard.

findings.evidence: friend easy to read error messages
findings.rationale: 'friend easy to read' (apparently intended as 'friendly, easy to read') is subjective and unquantified with no objective readability or tone criteria.

findings.evidence: consistent symbols and colors for clear notifications
findings.rationale: 'consistent' and 'clear' are subjective terms without a defined visual convention or standard mapping of symbols and colors to notification states.

findings.evidence: easily updatable
findings.rationale: 'easily updatable' is subjective and unquantified, providing no testable criterion for update effort, steps, or downtime.

findings.evidence: the site
findings.rationale: Refers to the product as 'the site' instead of using the established product name 'Web Store' from GJ-001, GJ-002, and GJ-005.

findings.evidence: easy to upgrade
findings.rationale: 'easy to upgrade' is subjective and unquantified, offering no measurable maintainability criterion.

findings.evidence: extremely portable
findings.rationale: 'extremely portable' is subjective and unquantified, lacking measurable portability criteria.

findings.evidence: the usb drive
findings.rationale: Uses the term 'the usb drive' for the USB hardware appliance previously termed 'the USB system' in GJ-009 and GJ-010.

findings.evidence: easy to migrate or backed up
findings.rationale: 'easy' is subjective and unquantified, giving no testable threshold for migration or backup effort or duration.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses non-binding modal 'should' instead of 'shall', making it unclear whether debug mode support is mandatory or optional.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses non-binding modal 'should' instead of 'shall', leaving mandatory compliance for test credit card transactions unclear.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses non-binding modal 'should' instead of 'shall', leaving mandatory compliance for test shipping orders unclear.

findings.evidence: should be able to
findings.rationale: Uses non-binding modal 'should' instead of 'shall', leaving mandatory compliance for creating a test environment unclear.

findings.evidence: weborder system
findings.rationale: Introduces a different product name ('weborder system') instead of the established name 'Web Store' from GJ-001, GJ-002, and GJ-005.

findings.evidence: The system hardware shall be fixed and patched via an internet connection.
findings.rationale: Uses passive voice without identifying which actor (e.g., Yoggie Corporation, Web Store developers, or administrators) performs remote hardware fixes and patches.

findings.evidence: coordinate on future enhancement and features with our organization
findings.rationale: 'coordinate on future enhancement and features' has no verifiable deliverables, process, or criteria, and 'our organization' is an undefined referent.

findings.evidence: OS: Apache web server
findings.rationale: Lists 'OS: Apache web server' (and groups OS/database software under hardware requirements), conflicting with GJ-002 which specifies Slackware Linux 2.6 as the operating system and Apache Web Server as the web server.
